clue.text: Execute our Charlie across the pond?

blocks.note: to execute a task is to do it
'our' means belonging to us, i.e. of us

explanation.surface: A grim suggestion to put to death an American friend named Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'charlie' is British slang for a fool; 'across the pond' asks for the American equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: Doofus is American slang for a stupid person, the US counterpart of calling someone a right charlie.

His was TWL, retiring to Parisian island

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the words before it are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: taken as written
île is French for island

explanation.surface: The author of TWL heads off to retire on an island in the Seine.
explanation.walkthrough: TWL is The Waste Land, the poem whose five parts are the puzzle's long answers; TOILE read backwards gives ELIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot wrote The Waste Land (1922), so his poem was TWL.

clue.text: Rage of Zyzzyva?

blocks.note: first meaning: the latest fashion, the thing all the rage
second meaning: zyzzyva, a weevil, comes at the very end of many dictionaries

explanation.surface: The fury of some strange creature called Zyzzyva.
explanation.walkthrough: Zyzzyva is a tropical weevil whose name closes many English dictionaries; the question mark flags that it is being defined by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both the newest fashionable thing and, literally, the final entry in a dictionary.

clue.text: TWL's V: that with Hades swirling around below

indicators.note: swirling letters are churned up and come out in a new order
around means placed on either side of something, so the jumbled letters enclose the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
below and under are synonyms

explanation.surface: A literary note that part V of The Waste Land has Hades churning underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged thirteen letters split around UNDER to make the title.
explanation.definitionFit: What the Thunder Said is the title of the fifth and final section of Eliot's The Waste Land.

clue.text: Gold chain seen in bourse regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is taken
in places one piece inside the other, here the measure inside the chosen letters

blocks.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of bourse
CH is the abbreviation for a chain, an old unit of length

explanation.surface: A gold necklace spotted on the stock exchange floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold' and 'chain' look like a piece of jewellery; gold is the colour definition and chain is the surveyor's measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a yellowish-brown earth pigment, a shade close to golden yellow.

clue.text: Cornish banker in decline spared last pound

indicators.note: spared means let off or done without, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: a decline is a fall
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A Cornish bank manager in hard times was spared losing his last pound.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is a river, something with banks; the Fal flows through Cornwall to Falmouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fal is a river in Cornwall, and a river is a thing with banks, hence a banker.

clue.text: Monk runs to be entered in a Derby?

indicators.note: to be entered in means going inside something else, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a derby is a bowler, a type of hat
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A monk runs and is entered as a competitor in the Derby horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the Derby here is the hat (an American name for a bowler), not the race at Epsom.
explanation.definitionFit: An arhat is a Buddhist saint or monk who has attained enlightenment.

clue.text: He's in for playing with singular metre in TWL's III

indicators.note: playing with things moves them about, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the word metre in the singular, taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet is in for some fun experimenting with an unusual metre in part III of The Waste Land.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fire Sermon is the title of the third section of The Waste Land, named after a Buddhist sermon.

clue.text: Mum in Blockbuster a female returning holy book

indicators.note: returning means coming back the way it went, so the words before it are read backwards
in places the parent word inside the reversed string

blocks.note: a blockbuster is a big hit
taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother appears in a blockbuster film about a woman coming back to scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mushaf of Fatimah is a scripture revered in Shia tradition, named for the Prophet's daughter; the clue lets her name stand for the book.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shia belief the Mushaf Fatimah, often just called Fatimah, is a sacred text, loosely a holy book.

clue.text: Old court letter's content and composition

indicators.note: the content of something is what lies inside it, so the outer letters are dropped

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
CT is the abbreviation for court
the inside letters of letter

explanation.surface: Something about the contents and composition of a letter from an ancient court.
explanation.definitionFit: An octette is a musical composition for eight voices or instruments, a variant spelling of octet.

clue.text: Moved quickly to secure vessel abandoned

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the first word wraps around the second

blocks.note: sped is past tense of speed
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: Someone rushed to tie up a boat that had been left adrift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship that has been abandoned; it is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurned means rejected or cast aside, just as something abandoned has been left behind.

clue.text: Svenson say is an eccentric in little plane?

indicators.note: eccentric means odd and out of the ordinary, so the letters before it are put in an unusual order

blocks.note: Bo Svenson is an actor; 'say' shows his first name is wanted by example
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is the actor Bo Svenson an oddball for flying in a tiny aircraft?
explanation.walkthrough: The 'plane' is the plane tree, not an aircraft; a plane can be grown in miniature as a bonsai.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai is the art of growing dwarf trees in pots, and a plane tree could be one, hence a little plane.

clue.text: Drink from west in view, Ram's Head receiving order raised

indicators.note: in places the direction inside the word for a view
raised in a down clue means read upwards, so the word is reversed
the head of a word is its first letter
receiving means taking something in, so the reversed word joins before the head letter

blocks.note: to view is to see
W is the abbreviation for west
an edict is an order
first letter of Ram

explanation.surface: A drink from the West Country, with a ram's head on view as the order is raised.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet cider is a fermented apple drink made with less sugar converted to alcohol.

clue.text: Bats left to fate here, Buddha saving one: TWL's I

indicators.note: saving means keeping something safe inside, so the Buddha holds a letter
bats as an adjective means crazy, so the letters that follow are scrambled

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Bats are left to fate here while a Buddha rescues one creature: a scene from part I.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' looks like the animals; it is the anagram signal. BUDDHA with I inside joins L and TO FATE HERE before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Burial of the Dead is the title of the opening section of The Waste Land, from the Anglican funeral service.

clue.text: Reckon D notice should come first

indicators.note: should come first is an ordering instruction, putting the notice ahead of the letter it follows in the clue

blocks.note: an ad is a notice; 'should come first' puts it before the letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A D-notice is a British government request not to publish, and it should take priority.
explanation.walkthrough: A D-notice is a UK government request to the press not to publish something; here the phrase splits into the letter and a notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To add is to reckon up or calculate a total.

clue.text: Hard to stop enemy with Trumpian slogan upping tax in TWL's II

indicators.note: upping in a down clue sends the words upwards, so they are read backwards
to stop a thing is to plug it, so the letter goes inside the word for a tax

blocks.note: a foe is an enemy
Make America Great Again, Donald Trump's slogan
a cess is a tax or levy
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: It's hard to stop an opponent whose Trump slogan raises taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Game of Chess is the title of the second section of The Waste Land.

clue.text: Virtuous sort with a drop hidden away

blocks.note: a saint, abbreviated St, is a virtuous sort
taken as written
to shed is to drop, as with leaves

explanation.surface: A good person with a small drink has secretly put it out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Stashed means stored in a secret place, put away out of sight.

clue.text: Haggard heroine managed to net fish for playwright

indicators.note: to net is to catch in a net, so the word for managed surrounds the fish

blocks.note: She is the novel by H. Rider Haggard, named after its heroine
to run is to manage
the id, or ide, is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A worn-out heroine managed to catch a fish for a dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' looks like an adjective meaning gaunt; it is the novelist Rider Haggard.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Brinsley Sheridan was the Irish dramatist who wrote The Rivals and The School for Scandal.

clue.text: Seer contributing to Crome Yellow

indicators.note: contributing to means forming part of, so the letters are found inside the following words

blocks.note: the end of Crome and start of Yellow

explanation.surface: A prophet played a part in Aldous Huxley's novel Crome Yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seer' suggests a prophet, but it is literally a thing that sees.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye is the organ of sight, so it is literally a seer.

clue.text: Was fitting American with desire for wealth

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
greed is a desire for wealth

explanation.surface: A greedy American's behaviour was appropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that agreed were consistent or suited each other, as food agreed with someone.

clue.text: See 25
Church supporting Navy woman in difficult separation

indicators.note: supporting means holding up from beneath, and in a down clue the lower piece comes second

blocks.note: a Wren is a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A churchgoing naval woman supports her through a tough breakup.
explanation.walkthrough: Wrens were members of Britain's Women's Royal Naval Service.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrench is a painful parting, such as leaving home or a loved one.

clue.text: Maybe an old idea slightly altered on mixed dish

definitions.text: Maybe an old idea slightly altered

blocks.note: re means on or about, regarding
hash is a dish of chopped mixed ingredients

explanation.surface: Perhaps a leftover notion changed a bit, served over a jumbled plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehash is old material presented again with minor changes, so an old idea reworked is one example.

clue.text: TWL's IV's what betrayed criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is wrong or crooked, so these letters are bent out of shape

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Part IV of The Waste Land is what exposed the lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'what' after the apostrophe-s is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Death by Water is the short fourth section of The Waste Land, about the drowned Phlebas.

clue.text: Forming a unit see unit formed

indicators.note: formed means shaped into something, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to observe how a unit has been put together.
explanation.definitionFit: En suite is French for 'in sequence', describing rooms that connect to form a single set.

clue.text: See 7
Chicken is served with rook hearts and hock

indicators.note: served with suggests a dish flanked by accompaniments, so two letters go on either side

blocks.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook
a hen is a chicken
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A recipe: chicken served with rook hearts and ham hock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hock' looks like a cut of meat in this menu; it is the German wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock is white wine from the Rhine, and Rhenish is an old name for Rhine wine.

clue.text: Kahlo say delivered in fits and starts?

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so the first letters of the preceding words are taken
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: first letters of fits and and
to deliver someone from a thing is to rid them of it

explanation.surface: Did the painter Kahlo give birth in fits and starts?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fits and starts' reads as a phrase, but the starts are the initials of the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Frida is the first name of the Mexican painter Frida Kahlo; 'say' marks her as an example.

clue.text: Character spoken for leaves to make drink

indicators.note: spoken means said out loud, so the sound of the letter is wanted

blocks.note: a character is a letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A spokesman figure goes off to brew something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb meaning departs; it is the noun, dried leaves for brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is the dried leaf of the tea plant, infused in hot water to make a drink.
